observations: Live reproduction on the unfixed production daemon (cited from the architect): production state.json at 03:14 UTC had phases[LEGION-37]=implementer while the tester was the assigned phase, after the implementer's --resume relaunch re-registered.

A phase worker whose /worker/started falls into a daemon-down gap (the deliberate main->branch swap in (d)) stayed alive without registering until the boot watchdog's 3 alive-but-unconfirmed intervals retired and relaunched it; pre-existing boot behaviour, outside this issue.
loadState migrates in memory and writes only the .bak; disk state.json is rewritten on the first save after boot (for a few seconds it still read version 24). Pre-existing migration design.
Not hit on this run: the LEGION-39 negotiate_protocol timeout on a --resume relaunch; the LEGION-11 boot-time revokeSessionCapability TypeError (no dead confirmed worker at either restart).

Tester-side trap (not a code finding): with the profile's pi-legion-envoy 1.17.0 text-injected LEGION_GRANT preamble, a model that repeats the injected preamble in its own later commands shadows the fresh grant with a stale one and every `legion gh`/credential call 403s ('Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT'); the fix is to emit commands without the preamble.
